name: Timeline of organisation theory
purpose: How did thinking about organisations evolve?

parts.label: 1970– · Motivate through culture
points: Weick, March, Ouchi, Crozier, DiMaggio & Powell

apply: Place any author of the course in one quadrant to show his view of people and environment
pitfalls: Mixing up the axes: system (closed/open) is about the environment, individual (rational/social) about people

name: Fayol's 14 principles of management
purpose: How should managers run an organisation?

parts.label: Interest of the organisation
points: Subordination of individual interest to the general interest

apply: Check which principles a case firm follows or violates (e.g. a matrix breaks unity of command)
pitfalls: Forgetting that Fayol also defines 6 functions and 6 qualities of the manager
example: Mining context: danger made unity of command and good supervisors vital.

name: Weber's three types of legitimate authority
purpose: Why do people obey an authority?

parts.label: Rational-legal
points: Stable, impersonal rules – obey the function

apply: Identify the source of a leader's authority in the case and what happens when it is challenged
pitfalls: Real leaders often combine several types – say which one dominates

name: Weber's bureaucracy
purpose: What makes the bureaucratic ideal type efficient – and what goes wrong?

parts.label: Principles
points: Selection on qualifications, appointment, fixed salary

parts.label: Drawbacks
points: Complex rules and chains of command

pitfalls: Bureaucracy is an ideal type, not a description of every administration

name: Taylor's scientific management
origin: Taylor (1911), The Principles of Scientific Management
purpose: How to replace empirical management by an efficient system?

parts.label: Selection & pay
points: Right man in the right place

apply: Look for vertical (design vs execution) and horizontal (task) division of labour in the case
pitfalls: Taylor's functional foremen contradict Fayol's unity of command
example: Today: fast food, call centres, warehouses.
